headline: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event launches HomeView, refreshed Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini
summary: At its October 13 'Welcome Home' event, Apple launched the $299 HomeView smart display, a refreshed Apple TV 4K with hands-free Siri microphones, an updated $149 HomePod mini, and the Apple Home Collection of smart-home accessories made with LG and Schneider Electric, after earlier reports named only LG. Outlets disagree on whether the HomePod mini's Siri AI works at launch or arrives later.

claims.statement: Apple hosted a 'Welcome Home' smart-home event in New York on October 13.

sources.quote: Apple has just announced a new October event, taking place in New York on October 13th at 9AM ET.
Apple’s October 13th launch event — given the tagline “Welcome Home” — is all about its efforts for the smart home.

claims.statement: Apple unveiled HomeView, a 7-inch smart display that acts as a smart-home hub, priced at $299.

sources.quote: Two versions will be available in November for $299.
Apple’s first smart display is the 7-inch HomeView for $299

claims.statement: Apple refreshed the Apple TV 4K with far-field microphones for hands-free Siri and Find My support in the remote.

sources.quote: Apple is introducing a refreshed Apple TV 4K today with a pair of interesting new hardware features: far-field microphones to talk to Siri hands-free and Find My built into the remote.
New microphones, a new remote and the new Siri AI are on the company's streaming box.

claims.statement: The new Apple TV 4K costs $299 and will be available November 13.

sources.quote: The new Apple TV 4K costs $299, comes with Siri AI, and will be available on November 13.

claims.statement: The new Apple TV 4K costs about $100 more than the 2022 model it replaces.

sources.quote: Apple TV 4K 2022 vs. 2026: What's new and is it worth the $100 jump?

claims.statement: Apple refreshed the HomePod mini with a new chip and a 'SoundGlow' visual feature, priced at $149 and available starting October 30.

sources.quote: The new $149 HomePod mini with Siri AI and a 'SoundGlow' visual feature will be available starting October 30.

claims.statement: The HomePod mini's Siri AI features are not available at launch and are coming later.

sources.quote: Apple announces the HomePod Mini 2, but it isn’t ready for Siri AI at launch
The new model arrives on October 30, but its Siri AI features are coming later.

claims.statement: TechCrunch described the new HomePod mini as launching 'with Siri AI.'

sources.quote: The new $149 HomePod mini with Siri AI and a 'SoundGlow' visual feature will be available starting October 30.

claims.statement: Apple launched the Apple Home Collection, smart-home accessories including cameras, thermostats and door locks, made with LG and Schneider Electric.

sources.quote: Apple has partnered with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric to launch the Apple Home Collection, an assortment of smart home devices meant to be easy to set up and use.
Apple collaborated with LG and Schneider Electric on products that work with its HomeView display.

claims.statement: Before the event, reports said Apple was partnering with LG alone on the new smart-home accessories.

sources.quote: Apple and LG team up on new smart home gear, starting with a lock, doorbell, and thermostat
Apple is reportedly partnering with LG to launch a smart lock, thermostat, and doorbell

discrepancies.explanation: TechCrunch's lede frames the HomePod mini as launching 'with Siri AI,' while The Verge and Engadget state its Siri AI features are not ready at launch.

quotes.quote: The new $149 HomePod mini with Siri AI and a 'SoundGlow' visual feature will be available starting October 30.
Apple announces the HomePod Mini 2, but it isn’t ready for Siri AI at launch

discrepancies.explanation: Reports before the event named LG as Apple's only hardware partner, but the actual Home Collection launch credited both LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

quotes.quote: Apple is reportedly partnering with LG to launch a smart lock, thermostat, and doorbell
Apple has partnered with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric to launch the Apple Home Collection, an assortment of smart home devices meant to be easy to set up and use.
